description: SpaceX has the option to buy Cursor for $60 billion - or pay $10 billion to walk away. 💻🚀 The structure makes sense when you map what each side needs: Cursor needs compute to train frontier models, xAI needs developer interaction data to improve Grok.  #cursor #spacex #elonmusk #coding #ipo
_transcript: Let's talk about that SpaceX cursor deal because yesterday SpaceX announced that it has bought the right to acquire Cursor for $60 billion later this year or pay $10 billion and walk away. So the big question is why in the world would a rockets company want to buy an AI coding startup? Cursor is one of the most popular AI code editors on the market. It was founded back in 2022 and it was known for getting to $100 million in annual recurring revenue in under two years. Their most recent valuation from November was around $30 billion. But Cursor has a structural problem where it is currently bottlenecked by compute. In order to compete at the frontier against a cloud code or a codex, you need to train your own model. But unfortunately, a frontier training run costs somewhere around $5 billion in compute. So Cursor is in this sort of awkward position where it resells access to cloud and GPT models to its own users, all while those same companies are rolling out direct competitors to their product. XAI on the other hand has the opposite problem. If you remember Musk had merged SpaceX with XAI back in February and XAI had Colossus which is one of the most powerful supercomputers ever built However they have all this compute but not really a good coding product or application to route all of that infrastructure to. Plus, 10 of XAI's 12 original co-founders have since left the company. So together, this deal allows Cursor to run training jobs on Colossus with access to compute it usually wouldn't be able to afford on its own. And for XAI, they get very valuable cursor data. On top of this, we know that SpaceX is currently targeting a June listing for its IPO at a $1.75 trillion valuation. So adding something like a cursor to the portfolio before the roadshow gives them a much more solid enterprise software story alongside the rockets and the satellites. The way this entire deal is structured with the call option is pretty unusual, but it does give SpaceX a lot of strategic flexibility while cursor gets compute dependence and a cash injection of sorts without having to dilute themselves with metric funding. And either way, in the scenario that SpaceX's IPO doesn't go as well as expected and that $60 billion price tag becomes a lot more expensive, or if Cursor's growth stalls, then they'll have the $10 billion pay and walk scenario to fall back to.

description: This AI runs the whole recruitment process #hrautomation #aitools #hrtech #nocode #aiagent
_transcript: Watch this AI agent I built for HR recruiters. It helps them manage job applications automatically. I created it using BotPress and Make.com. Here's how it works. It all starts with an autonomous node. That's what allows the agent to make decisions and perform the right actions. Then I added a prompt that guides it to collect the applicant's job position, full name, email, and resume. The agent can also answer general questions using the company's knowledge base. When it answers, it follows a specific tone and guidance to keep everything consistent and professional. Once the applicant finishes the form, the agent creates a personalized confirmation email that will be sent automatically later. After that, I added a search knowledge card. This gives the agent access to information like open job positions, HR policies, and company details. When all the application data is ready, the agent sends it to a sub-workflow called Send Application Data. That sub-workflow makes an API call to make.com and sends all the collected information. In make.com, the data arrives through a webhook. Then, an HTTP module downloads the resume file, uploads it to a Google Drive folder, and saves all the applicant's details, like their full name, email, and Google Drive link, into Google Sheets. At the same time, the applicant receives a personalized confirmation email, created by the AI agent on Botpress, and the HR recruiter gets a message with all the applicant's details. Everything runs smoothly and automatically. Applicants get instant confirmation, and recruiters have all the data neatly organized in one place. If you'd like to see more AI automations like this, make sure to follow for the next one.

description: ​Using AI to earn a modest income of $10 per month is a very achievable goal. The key is to leverage AI tools to create a product or service that you can sell, or to improve your efficiency in a way that allows you to take on more work. Here are some of the most common and accessible ways to do it, broken down into different categories. ​1. Content Creation and Freelancing ​AI can significantly speed up the content creation process, allowing you to produce more work and earn more money on freelance platforms or through your own content.   ​AI-Assisted Writing: Use tools like ChatGPT, Jasper AI, or Writesonic to generate blog posts, social media captions, ad copy, or product descriptions. You can then sell this content on platforms like Upwork, Fiverr, or PeoplePerHour. A few short articles a month could easily reach your goal.   ​AI-Generated Art: Platforms like Midjourney, DALL-E, or Stable Diffusion can create unique images from text prompts. You can sell these images on stock photo websites (like Adobe Stock or Shutterstock) or create and sell digital art prints on sites like Etsy or Redbubble.   ​AI for Social Media: Use AI to generate social media content calendars, post ideas, and even design simple graphics. You can then offer social media management services to small businesses, helping them maintain an active online presence.   ​AI-Powered Freelance Services: Enhance your existing skills with AI. For example, use AI to write a first draft of a resume or cover letter and then charge a fee to provide the final polish and customization. You can also use AI tools to create video scripts, voiceovers, or to automate parts of a web design project.   ​2. Creating and Selling Digital Products ​AI makes it easier than ever to create digital products that can generate passive income.   ​E-books and Guides: Use AI to help you outline, research, and write a short e-book or guide on a topic you're knowledgeable about. You can sell it on platforms like Amazon KDP.   ​Print-on-Demand: Use an AI image generator to create unique designs for t-shirts, mugs, or posters. Then, use a print-on-demand service (like Printful or Redbubble) to sell them without needing to hold any inventory. You earn a small profit on each sale.   ​Selling AI Prompts: If you get good at crafting detailed and effective prompts for AI image or text generators, you can sell them on marketplaces dedicated to prompts.   ​3. Monetizing AI-Enhanced Websites or Channels ​Affiliate Marketing: Create a simple blog or a YouTube channel using AI to help with content creation. For example, use AI to write articles or video scripts about a specific product. Then, add affiliate links to that product. If someone buys through your link, you earn a commission.   ​AI-Generated YouTube Videos: You can use AI tools to generate video scripts, create AI-powered voiceovers, and even create simple animated visuals. Upload these videos to a YouTube channel and monetize with ads or affiliate links once you meet the platform's requirements.   ​The key to success with any of these methods is to add your own "human touch." AI can be a powerful assistant, but the most successful projects will be those that you edit, refine, and customize with your own creativity and expertise to ensure they are high-quality and unique.  . . . . . .  #makemoneyonline #foryoupage #tiktokusa🇺🇸 #foryoupage #sidehustle

AI art is sometimes the only way people with disabilities and people who were born with no talent can make art. I have no artistic talent, but I love the feeling I get when I'm creating art. That may be true, but people with disabilities can see their dream stories coming alive with AI writing. There are a lot of people who had COVID that now have brain fog and want to see their stories in print but can't type them out because of the brain fog. And there are people with dyslexia who have great stories in their heads but just need a little help with the words. And then there's me with ADHD who can't focus for more than a second, so I procrastinate endlessly from sitting down to write the stories I want to. So before you condemn AI art entirely, remember, this is the only way some of us can get that great feeling from making art.

description: The Evolution of AI-Generated Video: From Simple Experiments to Cinematic Reality Artificial Intelligence has transformed many areas of technology, but one of the most fascinating developments has been the evolution of AI-generated video. Over the years, AI videos have evolved from simple, low-quality experiments into highly realistic productions that can look almost identical to real footage. This progress has been driven by advances in computing power, machine learning, and neural networks, as well as the work of companies such as OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Runway. ⸻ Early Stage: Basic Computer Animation (1960s–2000s) In the early days, computers could only create very simple animations. These were not truly created by AI but by rule-based programs. Programmers had to manually define every movement and action. The computer simply followed instructions and could not learn or improve on its own. Videos created during this time had very low resolution and unrealistic movement. Characters looked robotic, and environments were simple and artificial. However, these early experiments were important because they showed that computers could create visual content. During the 1990s and early 2000s, motion capture technology improved digital animation. Motion capture allowed computers to record real human movements and apply them to digital characters. Even though this improved realism, the computer still depended completely on human input. ⸻ The Rise of Machine Learning (2000s–2015) A major breakthrough happened when machine learning became more advanced. Instead of following fixed instructions, computers could now learn from large amounts of data. Neural networks allowed AI systems to recognize patterns in images and videos. During this period, AI became capable of recognizing faces, tracking objects, and improving video quality. It could also predict motion and understand visual information better. Platforms like YouTube began using AI to analyze videos and recommend content to users. However, AI was still mainly used to analyze videos rather than create new ones. This stage was important because it gave AI the ability to understand visual content, which was necessary before it could create its own videos. ⸻ The Deepfake Revolution (2016–2020) Around 2016, a new technology called Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) changed everything. GANs use two neural networks that compete with each other. One network generates images or video, while the other tries to detect errors. This competition helps the system improve quickly. This led to the creation of deepfakes, where AI could replace faces in videos with realistic results. For the first time, AI could create human faces, expressions, and movements that looked real. This was a major turning point. AI was no longer just analyzing videos—it was generating new content. However, deepfakes also created ethical concerns. People worried about misinformation, fake videos, and identity misuse. This led to discussions about regulation and responsible use of AI technology. ⸻ Modern AI Video Generation (2021–Present) Today, AI can generate complete videos from text descriptions. This technology is called text-to-video generation. A person can simply type a description, and the AI creates a video based on that prompt. Companies like OpenAI, Runway, and Stability AI have developed powerful systems capable of creating realistic video scenes. Modern AI video systems can now create: 	•	Realistic humans 	•	Natural movement 	•	Detailed environments 	•	Realistic lighting and shadows 	•	Smooth camera motion These systems can generate videos without cameras, actors, or physical locations. This has made video creation faster, cheaper, and more accessible. Thanks @Grok @Grok For helping us grow and making our videos. _transcript: When most people think about AI, they picture a sci-fi dystopian future with man versus machine. To me, it's the contrary of that. AI enhances and even supercharges humanity. Let me explain why. If you think about the core setup of AI, the algorithms need data and data needs humans. To ensure data is accurate, an expert human is often required. Only humans can understand the context and nuance to properly annotate the data to be fed to algorithms. Humans are the ones who teach the algorithms what to do. They're the ones making the decisions. They guide them, if something happens, here's what you should do, and the AI learns from that and replicates it. Unlike the movies, AI developers aren't focusing their attention on building replacements for humans. They're building tools to help free up our time and energy to focus on what humans can uniquely solve.
_evidence: AI enhances and even supercharges humanity

description: Engineering for Vibe Coders: Evaluating AI-Generated Code Just because AI-generated code works does not mean it is good. This is one of the biggest traps in vibe coding. You ask for something, the AI gives you code, you run it, and it works. So you move on. But here is the problem. Working code can still be wrong. It might miss edge cases. It might not scale. It might introduce security issues. Or it might just not fit the rest of your system. And over time, those small issues stack up. Now your codebase is inconsistent, harder to debug, and harder to change. The goal is not to slow down. It is to evaluate quickly. Ask simple questions. 1) Do I understand what this does? 2) Does it match my existing patterns? 3) What happens with bad input? If you do not evaluate AI-generated code, you are not moving fast. You are just borrowing problems from the future. Link in comments #ai #vibecoding #coding #programming

description: Vibe coding is fun. Even addicting. You prompt, iterate fast, and ship AI apps just because you can. Then move on to the next idea. The problem? That is how you make slopware — tools that technically work but solve nothing. So nobody uses them. Here's why vibe coding might not be the best approach for product managers: - It skips straight to a solution without asking why it should exist. - It mistakes your own pain point for everyone's problem. - It adds whatever AI can generate, not what users actually need. - It happens in a vacuum, disconnected from your product plans and team. - It chases the rush of building while ignoring ownership, security, and maintenance If you care about serious product outcomes, building on vibes is not enough. You still need a clear problem to solve, real user input, and proof that what you are building actually matters. #vibecoding #slopware #aiapps #aicoding #nocode

_transcript: This is the future of AI-powered stores. What you're seeing is a coffee shop, but it's not just any shop, because this coffee shop has AI software running 24-7 in all their cameras. You see those green boxes? Each one of those is a customer, and the AI is monitoring how long each person has been sitting in the cafe. But here's what's crazy. It's also monitoring the workers. You can see it's tracking their movement with those squiggly lines and their productivity, like how many drinks each person has served per hour. The software is called NeuroSpot, and it uses AI and machine learning to live track and analyze humans in physical stores. Now, of course, as a customer, my immediate reaction is shock and fear. It feels super weird to know you're being tracked everywhere you go. But as a business owner, having access to this level of real-time analytics could be super valuable. For example, if you ran a buffet, this software could immediately detect which areas were less popular, so you knew how to rotate the menu. Or if you ran a hardware store, you could study which aisles people linger the longest as a signal for confusion in signage and layouts. There are endless applications for this type of data. Not to mention CCTV AI, it'd be a lot harder to steal stuff. But the real reason this is so valuable is that this footage is going to be used to train robots. The best way for robots to learn is to watch humans complete the same task over and over. And because of that, I would not be shocked to see this type of AI camera software start popping up everywhere.
